svg.text: Concept-level diagram · All unconfirmed hardware marked TBD · Not a fabrication-ready wiring specification
Telemetry · status · faults · battery · LiDAR display
Raspberry Pi GPIO cannot drive motors directly.
Motor controllers must match the selected motors.
Independent of Pi, app, network, LiDAR
Not a substitute for software stop
Software Stop and communication watchdogs are additional protections, not substitutes
for a properly designed physical E-stop circuit.
Real-robot runtime — proposed, not yet implemented
Simulator must continue to run without energizing motors.
Solid thin = command/data · Dashed = feedback or regulated power · Thick solid = main power · Thick red = emergency stop
• This is a concept-level architecture. It is NOT a fabrication-ready wiring specification. Verify every connection against the actual device manuals before energizing.
• Raspberry Pi is a high-level controller only. It cannot and must not drive motor power directly. Motor controllers must be selected to match the motors and control interface.
• The physical E-stop must act on motor-power isolation hardware (contactor or equivalent) and must not depend on the Pi, app, network, or LiDAR.
• Lost or stale control commands must trigger a defined safe-stop behavior. Watchdogs are required but are not a substitute for the physical E-stop.
• LiDAR has blind spots and is not safety-rated protective equipment. It cannot reliably distinguish every person from every other obstacle.
• Disassembled MAXSwerve modules must be inspected and identified before final wiring. Encoder wiring, controller models, and communication protocols are TBD.
• Fuse ratings, wire gauges, connector pinouts, and logic-supply voltage must be calculated from confirmed hardware specifications.
Operating sequence (numbered steps on the diagram)
User presses Summon, Return, or a manual-drive control in the phone app.
App sends the request to the bridge over Wi-Fi / LAN.
Bridge validates the request and forwards a movement intent to the Pi runtime.
Pi checks operating mode, command freshness, E-stop state, and sensor health.
LiDAR data informs obstacle detection and navigation. (Blind spots exist; not safety-rated.)
Motion controller calculates swerve targets and sends commands to motor controllers.
Motor-controller feedback and sensor status return to the Pi.
Pi forwards telemetry back through the bridge to the phone app.
Software Stop or watchdog requests motion cease. The independent physical E-stop disables motor power through its hardware circuit.
This diagram is a concept. Update using actual device manuals and specifications before energizing any real hardware.
